BiblicalUsage: To wrest is to bend justice out of shape — and this word covers every way of doing it. The Preacher says what is crooked cannot be made straight, Elihu insists the Almighty will not pervert judgment, Lamentations says the Lord does not approve when a man's cause is turned aside, and Amos exposes merchants who falsify the balances to cheat the poor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God notices twisted scales and twisted courts, and I believe that is good news for the poor. No one who wrests justice gets away with it forever, because the Judge himself cannot be wrested.
